title: Build a living system you can see
subtitle: A reader-first tour of Conduit, with the real Patchbay opened only when the work calls for it.

cover.invitation: Begin with the problem that made Conduit necessary, then build a visible, bounded program one connection at a time.

projects.title: Project one: Make the program visible
projects.description: Build a small continuous system whose components, connections, limits and meaning can be read as one program.

chapters.title: The program we could no longer see
chapters.description: Why a living system needs a visible topology before it needs more machinery.
chapters.opening: Conduit began as an attempt to see one behavior that had scattered across speech, sensors, models, services, motors, microcontrollers and computers.

sections.title: Recover the hidden program
sections.summary: Separate the program's promises from the machinery currently realizing them.

blocks.body: Picture one behavior that starts with a person and ends in software, sound or motion. The interesting thing is the whole path, not any one function call.
When that path dissolves into callbacks, processes, deployment files and private conventions, changing one implementation means rediscovering the program.
Name components, cords, contracts, placement, pressure and observation as parts of the program itself.
Open the compact lab and inspect a current checked ticker: a tiny system that starts once, waits, wakes, flows and remains alive.
The Patchbay and result are projections of the same checked source and exact run session; expanding the lab does not create a second example.
A realization may move or be replaced while the declared topology, contracts and bounded flow stay legible.
Which parts of one of your systems are truly the program, and which are only today's realization?
Next, make the smallest visible message path and witness its result.

chapters.title: Patch a first message
chapters.description: Turn source into a visible path, disturb it, repair it and inspect what actually ran.
chapters.opening: A useful first program is small enough to understand completely and real enough to fail honestly.

sections.title: Hello, panel
sections.summary: Create, conduct and display one bounded text value.

blocks.body: Start with one literal, one display and one cord.
Run the panel and read the result before opening its technical proof.
The visible result, plan and evidence belong to the same exact worker run.
Now break the path deliberately.

sections.title: Pull the cord
sections.summary: See an incomplete graph remain readable without pretending it can run.

blocks.body: A visual editor must keep invalid authored intent visible instead of silently inventing a runnable graph.
The unavailable Run control is part of the explanation, not an inconvenience to hide.

sections.title: Change the value, not the topology
sections.summary: Keep source identity and a local learner draft distinct.

blocks.body: A draft is local reading work; it is not authored source, a resolved plan or a surviving run.
Refresh can restore your text without claiming that the previous execution session survived.

sections.title: Ask how we know
sections.summary: Reveal exact plan and evidence only when the question requires them.

blocks.body: Read the action and result first, then open the proof drawers.
Progressive disclosure changes presentation, never the authority of the underlying records.

chapters.title: Read components and cords
chapters.description: Use ports, direction, types, fan-out and terminal states as explicit promises.
chapters.opening: A box and a line become useful only when their semantic responsibilities remain readable without color or motion.

sections.title: More than one port
sections.summary: Read each receiving and outgoing promise independently.

blocks.body: Ports are named semantic boundaries, not decoration on a node.
The textual port list follows the same projection as the visible faceplate.

sections.title: Direction is part of the promise
sections.summary: Reject a cord whose endpoints cannot satisfy receiving and outgoing roles.

blocks.body: A line between two boxes is ambiguous unless both endpoint roles are explicit.
The diagnosis remains in reading order even when the visual canvas is unavailable.

sections.title: Make fan-out a choice
sections.summary: Treat delivery multiplicity and pressure as semantics.

blocks.body: Duplicating a value is a node-level decision with bounded downstream delivery, not a free visual fork.
Types make the promise more precise.

sections.title: Types mean promises
sections.summary: Keep compatibility proof separate from visual proximity.

blocks.body: Nearby ports are not necessarily substitutable.
Compatibility comes from semantic contracts; the canvas only presents the proof or failure.

sections.title: Empty is not never
sections.summary: Read terminal state independently from the absence of a value.

blocks.body: No value yet, no value ever and an explicit empty value are different facts.
A bounded live system needs terminal meaning as much as it needs value meaning.

chapters.title: Compose a larger faceplate
chapters.description: Nest panels while keeping public jacks, internal realization and reusable meaning distinct.
chapters.opening: Composition should make a system easier to read without erasing how its public promises are realized.

sections.title: Put a panel in a panel
sections.summary: Compose a checked definition without copying its implementation.

blocks.body: Build a larger component from a smaller visible program.
Bring its useful promises to the front.

sections.title: Put the jacks on the front
sections.summary: Expose explicit public ports for a composite.

blocks.body: A composite's interface is a contract, not a leak of its private wiring.
Logical and expanded projections preserve the same source-backed identity.

sections.title: Inside / outside
sections.summary: Move between a public faceplate and its expanded realization.

blocks.body: Toggle the topology projection and follow the same semantic port across the boundary.
Source selection, logical ports and expanded ports remain linked by projected identities.

sections.title: Reuse without copying
sections.summary: Keep one definition and multiple exact realizations distinguishable.

blocks.body: Copying implementation text makes later replacement and proof harder.
Reuse should preserve meaning while exact plan identity records each realization.

sections.title: Observe a living value
sections.summary: Attach bounded presentation to a running system without turning it into a semantic cord.

blocks.body: Let the system remain alive between admitted wakes.
Watch is isolated instrumentation; semantic tee and recorder behavior remain plan-visible choices.

projects.title: Project two: Trust the running system
projects.description: Carry visible source through exact plans, bounded execution and evidence without confusing any of their identities.

chapters.title: Witness without rewriting history
chapters.description: Use Patchbay observation and exact records to explain what ran.
chapters.opening: Observation is trustworthy only when presentation never becomes execution authority.

sections.title: Let Patchbay observe Patchbay
sections.summary: Read bounded evidence from the same exact run shown in the workspace.

blocks.body: A teaching timeline must reveal executor evidence, not synthesize a friendlier history.
The compact result, expanded timeline and textual evidence table share one ordered record.

sections.title: Keep four records distinct
sections.summary: Separate source, plan, run and presentation while moving between them deliberately.

blocks.body: A source draft, resolved plan, exact run and Patchbay layout answer different questions.
Reading progress and local drafts can survive refresh; a live run cannot be inferred to survive with them.

reference.description: Search canonical checked panels by capability without entering the book's Previous/Next path.

cookbook.title: Cookbook
cookbook.description: Search focused recipes and open their exact lesson artifacts independently of the sequential book.

Build a persistent bounded HTTP service
Carry value, clock and feedback facts
Import contract packages without acquiring implementations
